# Saṅgahitakathā (Kv 7.1)

**ID:** Kv 7.1  
**Section:** Kathāvatthu (kv)  
**Collection:** Abhidhamma  
**Title (Pali):** Saṅgahitakathā  
**tipitaka.org (CST):** [https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/abh03m3.mul14.xml](https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/abh03m3.mul14.xml)

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Saṅgahitakathā* (Kv 7.1) is the opening debate of the seventh chapter of the *Kathāvatthu*, situated in the Abhidhamma Piṭaka. The discussion examines the thesis that "no phenomena are included within [or grouped together by] other phenomena" (*n'atthi keci dhammā kehici dhammehi saṅgahitā*, Kvu 335), a position attributed in the tradition to the Rājagirikas and Siddhatthikas [Dutt 1978; Jayatilleke 1963]. According to this view, there is no separate quality adhering to or attached to another (exemplified by analogies such as oil in mustard seed or feeling in perception), stemming from the corollary that consciousness alone functions without distinct accompanying mental states [Dutt 1978]. K. N. Jayatilleke identifies this as one of the earliest Buddhist philosophical discussions addressing the problem of universals, noting that the opponents rejected grouping mental phenomena under general categories by arguing that ideas cannot be linked together by other ideas like two oxen bound by a yoke or rope (*yathā dāmena vā yottena vā dve balivaddā saṅgahitā*, Kvu 336) [Jayatilleke 1963].

**Sources**

- [Dutt 1978] Nalinaksha Dutt, Buddhist Sects in India (1978) — Attribution of the thesis to the Rājagirikas and Siddhatthikas and doctrinal explanation regarding citta and mental states.
- [Jayatilleke 1963] K.N. Jayatilleke, Early Buddhist Theory of Knowledge (1963) — Discussion of the debate on grouping ideas, PTS page references (Kvu 335–336), the problem of universals, and the yoke-rope simile.
